doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Comedian mishaps with Milton Berle and Frank Gorshin
summary: He splits two drumheads on a Berle rim shot and tells of a mixed-up chart playing Turkey in the Straw for Gorshin.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Did you ever have any train wrecks along the way, that maybe necessarily weren’t your fault, but something happened?
I can remember breaking a drum head. I played for Milton Berle, who had a lot of music, as does Don Rickles. Comedians tend to have a lot of music. And he wanted a big rim © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

shot right at the beginning. And we practiced this rim shot during rehearsal. So I thought, boy it he going to get a rim shot, in a packed showroom. And I came from above my head with the butt of the stick, and came down on that drum head, and there was no saving it. I split the head completely across, which — no sound at all. And the only method I could think to get through the show was I turned the drum over and played on the bottom head, and I broke that too, because the bottom head is significantly thinner than the top. So how’d I get around that? Well I slid over my floor tom and did that. It didn’t have a great sound but I got through the show. Yeah that was an interesting show.
And the drummer, for comedians, you’re probably expected to do all the little kedda- boom-crash.

You have to be a mind reader. You almost have to second guess them. I think it’s probably something that any show drummer has to be is you have to be ahead. You have to be reading ahead, and thinking ahead what will happen. And if someone’s in trouble it’s almost like you have to save the show.
Man you really have to be on the top of your game and alert for those things.

You try and be. Things happen that are just beyond your control. I can remember doing a Frank Gorshin show, an impersonator, in Nassau. And the piano player was a jazz player but not really versed in playing shows. And when we did the rehearsal everything was okay. But he didn’t put the music back in order. And Frank does like a country/western impersonation, an Elliot Ness, and he reversed those two charts. So when he came out with the hat and did the Elliot Ness thing, he played “Turkey in the Straw.” And it didn’t go over well at all with Frank and he certainly let the band know afterwards. Although the audience thought it was funny. And later I found out that he actually instituted that into his show.
That’s opportunistic of him. If it gets a laugh, it must be good, right?
